highlights.title: Election Deniers Think the GOP’s Terrible Midterm Polling Is a ‘Psyop’
highlights.summary: Dozens and dozens of high profile MAGA influencers and pundits have weighed in. “The laughable fake polls are rolling out,” Catturd posted on X.
body: Taking their lead from president Donald Trump, election deniers have dismissed the GOP’s terrible polling numbers by claiming the polls themselves are fake, a psyop, or a ploy to stop Republicans from turning out to vote in November.
Kevin Roberts, president of the Heritage Foundation, a conservative think tank, told Fox News that midterm election polling is a “psyop…to depress conservative turnout.”
“The midterms are near,” Phillip Buchanan, the election denier and MAGA troll known online as Catturd, wrote to his four million followers on X. “The laughable fake polls are rolling out.”

For over a decade, Trump has claimed without evidence that American elections have been impacted by fraud. In the wake of his loss in 2020, an entire online community and ecosystem of election denial groups sprung up to push the baseless allegation that former president Joe Biden stole the election from Trump. These claims have become central to the Republican Party’s belief system, to the point where hundreds of GOP candidates for federal and statewide elections in November have expressed doubts about the integrity of US elections.

highlights.title: Don’t be fooled—LLMs don’t reason
highlights.summary: On an afternoon in Seoul in March 2016, I watched a program I helped build put a stone on the fifth line of a Go board in what looked like a gift to its human opponent. Move 37 in game two of the five-game match looked so absurd that some commentators thought it was a…
body: When Deep Blue defeated then reigning world chess champion Garry Kasparov in 1997, it did so by looking six to eight moves ahead per player and evaluating 200 million chess positions per second, using rules hard-coded by humans. Go is a vastly more complex game. A stone’s worth depends on how distant groups and territory unfold over dozens of moves. Computing even a fraction of the possible outcomes would take a supercomputer billions of years. To win, AlphaGo had to sense who was ahead at a glance and even invent moves no human had thought to play.

That is why many accounts of AlphaGo’s match against Lee portray move 37 as a flash of pure machine intuition. But that is a misunderstanding. It was actually AlphaGo’s powers of reasoning that made this creative choice—and these are powers that today’s AI lacks. If we want future AI systems to produce trustworthy results and really novel insights in fields like science and medicine, we need to equip them with genuine reasoning capabilities of this kind.

highlights.title: Disney President Reacts to Live-Action Moana Flop, Says It Was an 'Excellent Film' Hit by 'Unusual Circumstances'
highlights.summary: Disney president Dana Walden has blamed "unusual circumstances" for the live-action Moana movie's disappointing box office, and defended the project as an otherwise "excellent film." Speaking this week at the Bloomberg Screentime event (via Variety ), Walden framed Moana's poor performance as a…
body: "It's so competitive right now that you have to have... the right film at the right time, with audiences feeling a certain degree of demand," Walden stated. "I would say our live-action Moana, which is excellent, I think it was hurt by the proximity to our second animated version of Moana, which came together under unusual circumstances, but premiered about 18 months before this one."

The unusual circumstances Walden is referring to here relate to Disney's relatively last-minute pivot that saw Moana 2 change from launching as a Disney+ series to a theatrical movie. This resulted in the project being slotted into Disney's film schedule awkwardly just a year and a half before the long-gestating plans for a live-action film.
"Perhaps there was not enough time to create a lot of pent-up demand for another film," Walden concluded.

highlights.title: A Flaw in ChatGPT’s Mac App Could Have Let Hackers Grab Sensitive Data
highlights.summary: While the focus has been on AI agents’ hacking capabilities, a recently patched vulnerability in a ChatGPT app shows that AI software is itself an inviting—and vulnerable—target.
body: Hardly a day goes by lately without news of AI agents autonomously hacking websites or AI tools being used by cybercriminals and scammers. But a recently patched vulnerability in the macOS version of OpenAI’s ChatGPT underscores the potential value to attackers of compromising AI software itself as these apps proliferate more and more.

The bug could have been exploited to essentially take over ChatGPT on a victim’s computer, giving an attacker access to all the chat logs and other data stored by the app, as well as interconnections like browser sessions. Discovered by researchers at the Objective-See Foundation, the vulnerability illustrates the deep system access and trust that AI platforms are afforded in order to work—and the target that this puts on their backs.

“Agents need a lot of access to do their job,” says Objective-See Foundation software analyst and longtime macOS researcher Patrick Wardle. “They are like the building manager who has access to the keys to all the rooms. So if they can be corrupted or subverted, that’s super problematic. It can mean that unprivileged code could then potentially have access to all the things.”

highlights.title: 3 Questions: A new resource to empower young entrepreneurs
highlights.summary: Martin Trust Center Managing Director Bill Aulet introduces Dear Dreamer, a free platform for middle and high school students who want to learn about entrepreneurship.
body: The book “Disciplined Entrepreneurship” by Bill Aulet, managing director of the Martin Trust Center for MIT Entrepreneurship and the Ethernet Inventors Professor of the Practice at the MIT Sloan School of Management, walks readers through the 24 steps of starting a venture. With more than half a million copies sold, the approach has proven remarkably effective: MIT students who use the framework in the delta v startup accelerator program have a 61 percent survival/acquisition rate and have collectively raised over $3 billion dollars.

Dear Dreamer is open to all students in middle and high school. It adapts the disciplined entrepreneurship framework into a digital, self-paced learning experience featuring short educational videos, interactive exercises, and personalized feedback on the user’s idea. Aulet says the goal is to empower 50,000 young entrepreneurs by 2030.
MIT News spoke with Aulet about the mission of the project and how it came together.

body: PlayStation and Xbox have added age ratings to GTA 6 's store pages across several regions. This gives us some idea of what to expect from the game's more extreme content. Alongside its Mature rating in the United States, there were the following warning labels: blood and gore, intense violence, mature humor, nudity, strong language, strong sexual content, and use of drugs and alcohol.

These are the same labels seen on Grand Theft Auto 5 's store page, so it wasn't particularly alarming. highlights.title: Video Games Europe hits back at EU watchdog targeting King, Supercell, Mojang and more over IAP practices
highlights.summary: The EU’s Consumer Protection Cooperation Network has launched coordinated enforcement actions against games companies including King, Supercell, Mojang, Riot Games, Activision Blizzard and Ubisoft, over how they sell and handle in-game virtual currencies.
body: The CPC Network brings together national consumer protection authorities from across the EU and EEA and is coordinated by the European Commission. In a joint statement published September 30, it said it had found that “a high number of video game companies” had made no substantive changes to their practices since it published non-binding “Key Principles” on in-game currencies in March 2025, despite extensive subsequent talks with industry bodies.

It said the coordinated actions are particularly focused on compliance around variable reward systems such as loot boxes, “dark patterns” and other “harmful influencing techniques”, and practices that directly exhort children to spend money, which it says EU law already prohibits.
Video Games Europe and the European Game Developers Federation pushed back on the CPC Network’s actions in a statement also published on September 30.

highlights.title: A century after the weekend was invented, it has disappeared. Let’s reclaim leisure | Richard Morgan
highlights.summary: Henry Ford’s 1926 policy held for decades before eroding into a 24/7 mindset. Here’s what we can do about it. It was a Saturday. In fact, the Saturday. Almost exactly a century ago, on 25 September 1926, Henry Ford instituted a policy of weekends for his workforce.
body: It caught on, buoyed by portraits of leisure gracing the covers of the Saturday Evening Post, drawn by an idealistic young artist from New York named Norman Rockwell. In 1929, Walt Disney leveraged Saturday matinees of his animated films to launch The Mickey Mouse Club. On Saturday 25 June 1938, President Franklin Roosevelt passed the Fair Labor Standards Act, formalizing the weekend as federal policy.

Beyond workplace respite, the weekend began to form its own identity. In 1944, Frank Sinatra popularized Saturday as “the loneliest night of the week, because that’s the night my sweetie and I used to dance cheek-to-cheek”. And the 1948 lyrics to Tennessee Saturday Night blared: “Civilized people live there alright, but they all go native on a Saturday night.”

The postwar boom of suburban pleasures transformed weekends into an anchor of indulgence. Sábado Gigante in 1962. Saturday morning cartoons in 1963. The launch of TGIFriday’s as a singles bar in 1965. Super Bowl Sunday in 1967. And a banner year, 1969, saw the moon landing on a Sunday followed by a weekend of Woodstock.
points: Henry Ford’s 1926 policy held for decades before eroding into a 24/7 mindset.

highlights.title: Whatever AI Safety Is, It’s Not This
highlights.summary: Asking AI companies to self-regulate is a great way to pretend like you’ve accomplished something.
body: Here’s a fun history lesson for you. Don’t worry, we’ll make it quick! In 1966, nearly 51,000 people died on US highways. The overwhelming evidence suggested that many lives could have been saved with modern seat belts, which by then had been around for several years. The automotive industry responded by rallying together, and, in a triumph of self-regulation, voluntarily put the safety feature in every new vehicle that rolled off the line.

Kidding! Of course they didn’t do that. In the fall of 1966, Congress established the Department of Transportation and then passed the National Traffic and Motor Vehicle Safety Act as well as the Highway Safety Act, giving the federal government sweeping new authority to set safety standards. By 1968, seat belts were required in every new car. Despite a massive increase in highway traffic in the last 60 years, far fewer fatalities happen on the road today.
points: Asking AI companies to self-regulate is a great way to pretend like you’ve accomplished something.

highlights.title: PS5 gets "AI-guided upscaling" a bit like PS5 Pro's, and it's available now in Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei
highlights.summary: AI image upscaling is coming to PlayStation 5, Sony has announced, and it's available already in two games: Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei.
body: The image-upscaling technology is called Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR), and it's positioned as a slightly diluted or lesser version of the PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR), which is available on PS5 Pro - the "gold standard" of "AI-guided upscaling", Sony said on the PlayStation blog.

QSSR apparently provides improvements to image detail and "stability", courtesy of "a hand-tuned implementation that maximizes performance on PS5". In a comparison video for Marvel's Wolverine, the close-up image appeared fairly clear - detail is noticeably crisper with QSSR on.

"QSSR adds more pixel-level clarity and stability to our environments," Insomniac head of tech Mike Fitzgerald commented, "bringing out extra detail amidst the busy streets of Madripoor, the dense alleyways of Shinjuku, and many other areas across Logan's epic journey." It apparently "brings a great taste of the PS5 Pro experience" to players on PS5.

highlights.title: Olivia Dean accused of copying Bill Withers' Just The Two of Us
highlights.summary: The star's record label is sued over similarities between her song I've Seen It and Withers' classic.
body: British pop star Olivia Dean has been accused of copying the melody of Bill Withers' soul classic Just The Two of Us in a legal case filed in California.
The complaint centres around Dean's song I've Seen It, taken from her Brit Award-winning 2025 album The Art of Loving.

Just The Two of Us was a hit for Withers in 1981, and the publishers of the late singer's catalogue allege that the two songs "share musical features" that are "so striking" they cannot have arisen by coincidence alone.

The lawsuit names Dean's record label Capitol Records, parent company Universal Music Group and her publishing companies as the defendants. It does not seek damages from the singer herself or her co-writers Bastian Langebæk and Max Wolfgang.

highlights.summary: “InstructMesh” can generate designs for everyday objects that are easy to edit and fabricate for both experts and newcomers to 3D modeling.
body: “What you see is what you get” is a guiding principle for many software engineers — create programs where the content you’re editing looks the same as the final product. But when you’re using generative artificial intelligence systems to 3D print, say, a mug, you’ll likely get a cup that can’t hold your coffee. Why is that?

The issue is that AI models understand how an object should look, but not how it works, leading to impractical designs that undermine an item’s intended use. Even if you want to fix these errors, the models are typically hard to edit, especially for users new to 3D design.
points: “InstructMesh” can generate designs for everyday objects that are easy to edit and fabricate for both experts and newcomers to 3D modeling.

highlights.title: Avengers: Secret Wars Filming Delay Reports Spark Concern That Marvel's Multiverse Saga Finale May Be Postponed
highlights.summary: Reports of an Avengers: Secret Wars filming delay have sparked concern among Marvel fans that the movie's release date could be pushed back. This week, an array of Marvel movie insiders reported hearing that filming on Marvel's big Multiverse Saga finale will now begin later than planned, after…
body: Serial MCU tipsters Daniel Richtman, Alex Perez, and Apocalyptic Horseman appear to have independently verified that Secret Wars shooting will now take place early in 2027, likely in January, sparking concern among fans about the impact this hold up will potentially have.

It's worth making clear that Marvel is yet to give any official update on its production schedule, and it ultimately may not need to do so if there's no impact on Secret Wars' planned December 17, 2027 launch date. That said, the potential of the movie's shooting schedule changing has many fans questioning if the film can still be completed in time.

"Gives the cast time to promote Doomsday during this winter," Marvel fan BTSMGL wrote in one of several lengthy threads on reddit. "I'm not in a rush for Ghost Rider so as long as we get X-Men and BP3 still in 2028, I'm fine with this."

"A *lot* is riding on Doomsday," added vadermaulkylo. "They’re probably waiting to see how it's received before committing to anything. If Doomsday gets a bad critical and/or audience reception then that'll drastically change what they'd do in its second act film."

highlights.title: Health Care Workers Are Tired of Cleaning Up Palantir’s Mess
highlights.summary: A hospital giant and radiology network turned to Palantir to streamline scheduling, but nurses and other staff say the new software is causing errors, burnout, and frustration.
body: Over the past four months, Amber Retzloff, a critical care nurse in Florida, requested to work 50 specific 12-hour shifts. But over half the time, she says her hospital’s Palantir -powered scheduling software assigned her to different shifts, often putting her on back-to-back-to-back days and leaving her mentally drained. Retzloff doesn’t expect to always get the slots she wants, but by her count the tool does a far worse job honoring her preferences than managers did when they assigned shifts by hand.

Retzloff’s experience mirrors that of other nurses across HCA Healthcare, the largest hospital chain in the US. Since 2023, HCA has rolled out an AI scheduling tool it co-developed with Palantir called Timpani at roughly 130 of its 190 locations. Retzloff’s hospital adopted it nearly two years ago.

“No one is happy with Timpani,” says Retzloff, echoing what five nurses at other locations reported in interviews with WIRED. “Everyone complains all the time.” Other purported HCA workers have expressed similar gripes about the tool on platforms like Reddit.

highlights.title: Kim leads Asian Games seeking military exemption
highlights.summary: Tom Kim tops the men's leaderboard after the third round at the Asian Games as he seeks a gold medal that will significantly reduce the time he is required to spend in South Korea's military.
body: Having started two shots off the lead, Kim hit a brilliant five-under 65 that included five birdies and an eagle, taking him a stroke clear at 12 under par with one round to play.
Able-bodied South Korean males are usually required to undertake between 18 and 21 months of military service before the age of 28.
However the government rewards Asian Games gold medals and Olympic medals of any colour with a service exemption bar basic training, which lasts less than a month.
Athletes who have previously secured the exemption include former Tottenham footballer Son Heung-min, who served for only three weeks in 2020 having won the Asian Games two years earlier.

It included quests, companions, dialogue trees, Fallout’s iconic V.A.T.S. combat and even a working Pip-Boy.

The initial video, viewed 3.5 million times on X / Twitter, sparked a debate about the rights and wrongs of CHRIS FIRST’s use of AI, with some calling the game AI slop, and others impressed by the gameplay. As you’d expect, many responded to the video to predict that Bethesda would eventually step in, although CHRIS FIRST seemed somewhat naive to the situation.

“It’s all free and I make 0 money on it,” he tweeted. “I hope they don’t ask me to take it down. I really love Fallout and this was just a fun tech demo. But I should add a quest where you have to serve someone papers, but they keep running away.”

highlights.title: Europe's CPC targets King, Supercell, Mojang and others over virtual currencies
highlights.summary: Europe's Consumer Protection Cooperation Network is taking "coordinated actions" against a string of top games companies as it looks to investigate compliance with 'Key Principles' on in-game virtual currencies announced last year.
body: The CPC is a network of national authorities responsible for the enforcement of EU consumer protection laws. It has asked Activision Blizzard, Crytek, InnoGames, King, Mojang, Plarium, PLR Worldwide Sales, Riot Games, Supercell and Ubisoft to bring their commercial practices in line relating to in-game virtual currencies.

Games being assessed include Hunt: Showdown 1896, Forge of Empires, Candy Crush Saga, Minecraft, Mech Arena, Gardenscapes, Valorant, Clash of Clans, For Honor, Diablo Immortal and Call of Duty Mobile.

The games were selected for assessment by the CPC Network "in the context of a wide-scale market compliance check due to broad reach, cross-device accessibility, and varied age ratings, all of which amplify the impact of the practices on consumers".
It's not clear what, if any, 'Key Principles' have not been adhered to prior to the CPC Network opening its investigations.

highlights.title: Google’s new Guided Vision feature can help you read the fine print
highlights.summary: Guided Vision is launching in Gemini Live on compatible Android devices today to use AI to give real-time audio descriptions of anything you point your phone's camera at.
body: People with low vision can use Guided Vision to have Gemini describe what’s nearby and ask follow-up questions.

Like the VoiceOver Live Recognition feature Apple has added to the iPhone and Vision Pro, it’s designed for people who are blind, have low vision, or want assistance in specific situations. In addition to the Gemini app, Guided Vision is also available in Google TalkBack, or users can set up an accessibility shortcut for it in the Settings app on devices running Android 9 and above, after it was announced in a recent set of Pixel updates.

You can also ask follow-up questions about whatever you’re looking at, like asking Gemini to read off the expiration date on an item it helped you find. Google says Gemini will give you audio cues to help line up your camera if you ask about something that’s not in the shot. However, Google cautions users not to rely on Guided Vision for things like “navigation, safe-travel guidance, or obstacle detection,” or as a replacement for a cane or mobility aid.

body: The FA said the independent commission’s decision on City had “significant implications for the integrity of the game” and that it “will take action where appropriate.”

City intend to appeal against the verdict of the commission, who after a 42-hearing concluded the club had used a “Disguised Funding Scheme” and “sham contracts” to boost their income by more than £900m between 2009 and 2018.

The FA will wait until the appeal process has concluded, which based on the Premier League’s rulebook should be by the end of January, before deciding whether to take action but confirmed it was monitoring the case closely.
The FA also has powers to take action against individuals proven to have broken rules and/or acted dishonestly, which the commission concluded had been the case.

highlights.title: 31 Years Later, the Definitive Sci-Fi Cyberpunk Movie Is Free to Stream on YouTube
highlights.summary: Anime has never been short on landmark science fiction. Akira wrote the book on bridging cyberpunk and adult animation, while Neon Genesis Evangelion blended apocalyptic mech battles and psychological trauma into pure spectacle.
body: Yet for all the incredible science fiction anime the industry has produced, none has stared so directly into the unsettling future of synthetic identity and digital consciousness quite like Ghost in the Shell. Mamoru Oshii’s 1995 classic remains one of anime’s crowning achievements, influencing everything from 1999’s The Matrix to 2009’s Avatar, and there’s no better time to confront its bleak technological future than now, while it’s free to watch on YouTube.

Akin to some of my favorite shows — like Sonny Boy, Serial Experiments Lain, and Cowboy Bebop — Ghost in the Shell doesn't rely on high-octane action. Oshii lets audiences sit in silence more often than spectacle, letting you digest the on-screen outcomes and face some very dark perspectives on the nature of technology in an ever-evolving world. The director fills those moments with a smattering of neo-noir cyberpunk imagery, like crowded city streets, towering mega-buildings, neon-lit signs, rain-slicked windows, tangled wires dangling precariously overhead, floating carrier-filled skylines, and boats moving through polluted waterways.
